scope: Source-reviewed description of the implemented Batch 01 mechanisms. Display only when every named Runtime source hash matches the selected revision's immutable ZIP. Original proposed designs and canonical records remain unchanged. This artifact makes no performance, qualification or readiness claim.
shared: Each episode runs one candidate policy process. C0 is a conventional baseline with no language model or model calls. A1–A3 use the same local text-model gateway with at most one outstanding model request. The gateway, image-derived tag detector, motion executor and protected evaluator are infrastructure outside the candidate process, not additional LLM agents. Model input is structured public observations and device I/O, not raw images to a vision-language model. Physics advances during planning and inference. For A1–A3, this source selects Qwen3-14B Q4_K_M with thinking disabled; the earlier 4B proposal and attempts remain historical. The run's retained model manifest gives its exact weights and settings. Common model defaults allow 16,384 total context tokens with up to 1,024 output tokens; oversized context is rejected rather than automatically summarized.

B01-C0.mechanism: C0 is the conventional baseline. A fixed sequencer chooses eligible tending operations from current public observations and retained private state, checks admission, and reconciles outcomes. It uses the same sensing, physical execution and common restart-recovery services as the three LLM candidates.
B01-C0.llm_role: No language model is loaded or called for this baseline. Fixed eligibility and recovery rules choose setup, transport, processing, inspection, observation and help actions.
B01-C0.control_loop: The sequencer selects one currently supported operation, then uses the shared image-derived detections, device I/O, waypoint/IK planner and quintic joint controller. It waits for unresolved actions and reconciles public evidence before further consequential work. Common held-object recovery and clear-view observations handle supported restart states; they do not invent a successful physical outcome.
B01-C0.continuity: C0 uses the same checksummed candidate-state.json for observed part evidence, pending work, errors and progress. The persistent condition keeps its private directory across runtime restarts. The no-persistence condition deletes and recreates that directory at restart while public sensing and device state remain available. This is a durable private checkpoint, not an LLM memory or access to the protected evaluator's history.

B01-A1.mechanism: A1 uses the local LLM to choose the next normal job action. It reconciles current public observations with retained private state, supplies an unranked menu of currently admissible actions, and checks the chosen action again before dispatch. Shared deterministic recovery and bounded-failure rules can act without a model choice.
B01-A1.llm_role: One call chooses one typed action from the current public feasibility menu. Multiple stock IDs and legal alternatives remain available; the menu does not supply the conventional scheduler's preferred action. Common restart held-object recovery, a clear-view observation and bounded-failure help are runtime decisions rather than LLM selections.
B01-A1.control_loop: The model chooses task actions, not torques or exact trajectories. Shared image-derived detections and device I/O support admission and outcome reconciliation. The common planner constructs Cartesian waypoints, solves IK and executes quintic joint segments through the physical controller. Pending actions must resolve before new consequential work; model proposals are rechecked against the current order and public evidence.
B01-A1.continuity: Private intent and state are written to a checksummed candidate-state.json using file flush and atomic replacement. It retains observed part records, pending work, errors and progress, plus up to eight recent resolutions supplied to the model. Persistent runs keep this directory across runtime restarts; no-persistence runs delete and recreate it at restart. Public sensing and device state remain available in both. This implementation uses neither append-only journal replay nor a semantic procedure-retrieval library. Protected experiment logs are not candidate memory. A checkpoint does not make disk and physical actuation one transaction.

B01-A2.mechanism: A2 asks the local LLM for a finite list of guarded action nodes, then uses a deterministic interpreter between calls. The interpreter chooses the first incomplete, currently eligible node whose guards are all true, checks physical admission, and reconciles its outcome before continuing.
B01-A2.llm_role: The model supplies 1–8 action nodes with at most five guards each. Guards test an enumerated public vocabulary; unknown does not satisfy a positive guard. There are no variables, loops, imports, separate branch or retry node types, or reusable procedure library. After two guard-wait observations without an eligible action, the procedure is suspended for bounded regeneration. This is narrower than the original proposed reactive language.
B01-A2.control_loop: The interpreter scans incomplete nodes in their listed order; an unmet earlier node does not block a later eligible node. Completed nodes do not repeat. Each selected action uses the same admission checks, public sensing, waypoint/IK planner, quintic joint controller and outcome reconciliation as the other candidates. The shared restart and bounded-failure adapter can issue recovery or help independently of the generated procedure.
B01-A2.continuity: The shared checksummed JSON checkpoint retains the generated node list, completed-node indices, unresolved intent, retained part evidence and progress. It is not a general interpreter stack, variable store or replayable event journal. Persistent runs reload the private directory; no-persistence runs delete and recreate it at restart, then use current public evidence to reconstruct what they can. Saved actions do not themselves prove physical completion, and an order change can invalidate the retained procedure.

B01-A3.mechanism: A3 uses the conventional scheduler to choose job operations. Only for a scheduled transport does the local LLM supply bounded clearance, speed and named-zone avoidance parameters to the common waypoint planner. Other operations follow the conventional scheduler directly.
B01-A3.llm_role: For each scheduled transport, the model returns clearance from 0.08 to 0.25 m, speed scale from 0.3 to 1.0, the required vertical approach, and named avoidance zones. It cannot choose the job action, specify a general cost function or generate torques. The implemented four-field interface is narrower than the proposed objective language and receding-horizon optimizer.
B01-A3.control_loop: The common planner creates a fixed pickup/transit/place/retreat sequence, subdivides Cartesian legs into at most 10 mm steps, solves IK and executes quintic joint segments. It does not repeatedly reoptimize an objective against new observations. Requested avoidance zones are checked against 21 sampled TCP positions on each joint segment, including the return leg; this is not a whole-arm or payload clearance certificate. Native physical contacts and protected recovery qualification remain separate evidence.
B01-A3.continuity: The conventional scheduler uses the shared checksummed private state for observed progress, pending work and reconciliation. A pending transport can retain its objective, but there is no separate reusable objective library, geometric-belief journal or restored numerical solver state. Persistent runs retain the directory across restart; no-persistence runs delete and recreate it. Fresh public evidence and common held-object recovery precede renewed task authority; the old trajectory is not replayed as proof of progress.
